about.title: Personal Injury Help in Simi Valley, California
about.longDescription: Much of Simi Valley's daily traffic funnels onto a few routes: the SR-118 Ronald Reagan Freeway running the length of the valley, with Los Angeles Avenue, Cochran Street and Royal Avenue carrying the surface-street load. Public records for 2025, the most recent final year, list 357 injury collisions inside the city, 500 people injured and 5 traffic deaths. Those same records show reports tending to rise on Wednesdays between 5 p.m. and 7 p.m., as the evening commute moves off the freeway and onto local streets. If one of those numbers is you or someone in your family, the next steps can feel murky. Medical bills arrive before the insurance adjuster returns your call, and everyone seems to want a statement. We handle personal injury cases in Simi Valley, and we're here to help clear up the confusion. We work directly with clients on matters like car and motorcycle crashes, pedestrian injuries, falls and dog bites. Our team works on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery. You tell us what happened; we review your case and discuss your options with you. Whether to move forward is entirely your call.

whyChoose.title: What California Law Means for Your Simi Valley Claim

items.title: The clock runs two years, sometimes six months
items.desc: Most California injury claims must be filed within two years of the injury. If a city, county or state agency is involved, a claim may need to be filed in as little as six months, so it pays to ask early.

items.title: Being partly at fault does not shut you out
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault. If you share some blame, your recovery is reduced by your percentage of fault, but you are not barred from recovering.

items.title: No cap on pain and suffering in ordinary cases
items.desc: For a typical injury case in California, the law places no ceiling on non-economic damages such as pain, suffering and loss of enjoyment of life. An attorney can explain how those losses are documented.

items.title: Contingency means no upfront legal bill
items.desc: We work on contingency, taking a fee only if there is a recovery. Our initial consultation is free as well, so there is nothing to pay just to have a conversation.

items.question: Are you a law firm?
items.answer: We handle personal injury cases directly in the Simi Valley area. We do not provide legal advice beyond the scope of your case consultation. Any attorney-client relationship is between you and our team.

items.question: How long do I have to file an injury claim in Simi Valley?
items.answer: For most personal injury claims in California, the statute of limitations is two years from the date of injury. If a government entity is involved, such as a claim over a city-maintained road or vehicle, the deadline to present a claim can be as short as six months. Because those deadlines are strict, speaking with an attorney soon after the incident is wise.

items.question: Where do collisions in Simi Valley tend to occur?
items.answer: According to public collision records, the highest counts in Simi Valley are recorded along the SR-118 Ronald Reagan Freeway, Los Angeles Avenue, Cochran Street and Royal Avenue. Reports also tend to peak on Wednesdays between 5 p.m. and 7 p.m. These figures are neutral counts of where crashes have been reported, and higher volume on a corridor reflects the traffic it carries.

items.question: What if the crash was partly my fault?
items.answer: California uses pure comparative fault, so sharing responsibility does not eliminate your claim. Instead, any recovery is reduced by your assigned percentage of fault. An attorney can help you understand how fault might be apportioned in your situation.

items.question: What does it cost to get a case review?
items.answer: We offer a free initial consultation to discuss your case. Our team works on contingency, which means we are paid a percentage only if there is a recovery in your case. If there is no recovery, there is no attorney fee, and the specific terms are spelled out in a written agreement before you commit to anything.
